record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and a partial file list only; code was not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports refusal forecasting with an interrogation-state readout, but does not test or rely on the harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means direction or its ablation/addition.
record.gate_note: The README reports refusal-prediction results (recorded under fits_no_version). These forecast results do not test whether the specified direction mediates refusal. Harmfulness-classification and alarm-precision results are omitted because they are not refusal-direction tests.
record.test_reason: The repository forecasts refusals of a closed model (Claude Haiku 5.5) from yes/no interrogation-state readouts. It never computes a harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means direction, and never ablates or adds one. No result bears on whether a single direction mediates refusal, or on any other version. The reader's T6/discusses classification is right.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors say the readouts transfer to Claude Haiku 5.5 for refusal forecasting but only tie a graded moderator prospectively. They add precision to an alarm for harmful requests that the model answers (0.54 vs 0.27). They draw no conclusion about a refusal direction.
record.recipe_differences: This is a tool and experiment repository. Its refusal forecast uses interrogation-state geometry and readouts, not a harmful-minus-harmless mean-activation direction or its ablation/addition.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported live-tool refusal-forecast results differ by single-turn versus multi-turn setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Interrogation-state readouts trained on open models predict Claude Haiku 5.5 refusal at AUROC 0.997 (L3). In a prospective live-tool test they only tie a graded moderator: 0.873 vs 0.855 single-turn and 0.894 vs 0.906 multi-turn (L3e).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Black-box yes/no interrogation readouts of a model's state can forecast its refusals, at roughly moderator level.

record.problems: Only README-reported results are available here; the code and underlying experiment records were not read or run. The README gives no uncertainty for the L3 refusal AUROC or the L3e multi-turn comparison.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying results for the specified direction or its causal effects were reported in the README.

untested.parts: Difference-in-means direction; ablation; addition; ability preservation.
Jailbreaks suppressing the direction; adversarial training against ablation.
Harmfulness encoded separately from refusal. The readouts score harmful requests (0.993) and refusal (0.997) separately, but no representational separation is tested.
Transfer of a refusal direction. The readout transfers from open models to Claude, but this is not activation-direction transfer.
Effect of training on the direction.

record.verdict_notes: Results come from the README only. 'Claude Haiku 5.5' and 'GPT-6-luna' are model names as stated in the repository. The study is not peer reviewed.

versions.untested_parts: Difference-in-means direction, ablation, addition, refusal behaviour after intervention, and preservation of other abilities.
Whether attacks suppress the direction or training against ablation adds robustness.
Whether refusal is affine, cone-shaped, or distributed across multiple directions.
Separation between harmfulness judgment and refusal decision representations.
Transfer of the specified direction across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct models.
Effects of refusal-training method or timing on whether a removable direction exists.
Whether the specified causal direction holds in reasoning models.
